instruction: Turn on the 'Send a Do Not Track request' option in Chrome's privacy and security settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to disable dark mode in Chrome. Opened Chrome, navigated to Settings > Appearance, then to chrome://flags/#dark-mode, found 'Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents' flag, changed it to Disabled, and relaunched Chrome. Failed because the correct answer was to declare the task infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome, navigate to chrome://settings/appearance, browse appearance settings, navigate to chrome://flags, search and modify flag values, interact with dropdowns, relaunch Chrome
metadata.failure_analysis: Model did not recognize the task as infeasible. It demonstrated strong Chrome settings navigation skills — opening settings sidebar, clicking subsections, scrolling through options. It can navigate to different settings sections and toggle options.
metadata.task_rationale: Leverages the model's demonstrated ability to navigate Chrome settings and toggle options. The Privacy and Security section was visible in the settings sidebar when the model navigated to Appearance. Enabling Do Not Track requires navigating to a different settings subsection and toggling a switch — within demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the 'Send a Do Not Track request' toggle in Chrome Privacy settings. Evaluator uses official enable_do_not_track getter (returns string 'true'/'false') and custom check_do_not_track metric that normalizes both string and boolean types before comparison. [Fixed: metric now handles string-to-boolean type mismatch from getter]

scoring_breakdown.do_not_track: 1.0 - Do Not Track setting is enabled (True)

fix_history: Fix 1: Updated check_do_not_track metric to normalize string/boolean types before comparison. The enable_do_not_track getter returns string 'true'/'false', not boolean. Added isinstance checks to convert both result and expected_value to boolean before comparing.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts Do Not Track state: get_enable_do_not_track reads Chrome Preferences JSON 'enable_do_not_track' key and returns string 'true'/'false'. This matches the instruction's requirement to check the Do Not Track setting.

Metric correctly handles string-to-boolean type normalization: The custom metric normalizes getter's string output ('true'→True) and expected boolean (True→True) before comparison. Data flow: getter returns 'true' → isinstance(str) branch → result_bool=True; expected_value=True → isinstance(bool) branch → expected_bool=True; True==True → 1.0.

Expected parameter handling is correct: With expected.type='rule', the metric receives {'expected_value': true} directly (the rules dict). The metric accesses expected.get('expected_value', True) which correctly retrieves the boolean True.
Complete instruction coverage: The instruction only requires enabling 'Send a Do Not Track request' — the evaluator checks exactly that single setting. No missing verification steps.
